concept: SceneCard is a scene of the home, such as Movie night or Good night, printed on a small card of light stock that the person picks up and inserts into a room's Slot. The card is printing on a flat card one step lighter than the plastic, with the name on its top edge so it stays readable when the card stands half out of a slot, and it is never orange.

default_to_avoid.pattern: scene card grid of rounded tiles with gradient backgrounds and a big emoji, as in Google Home and SmartThings scenes
default_to_avoid.why_not: P6 forbids gradients and P1 keeps colour to one orange part per unit, so a scene is ink printed on plain light card stock and the room's own knob stays the only loud part.

default_to_avoid.pattern: scene card that runs the moment it is tapped, like a shortcut button
default_to_avoid.why_not: P3 asks that parts behave like parts, so a card is picked up and then inserted into one named slot, and the person always sees where the scene runs.

references.source: Yoto Player and its cards: content is chosen by inserting a printed card, which stands out of the slot with its picture readable
Braun and Ulm school punched and printed programme cards for appliances: function printed on card stock beside the machine
WCAG 2.2, 2.5.7 Dragging Movements: every drag has a single pointer and keyboard path that does the same

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The card is light card stock printed in dark ink in both themes, never orange, so the slot's unit keeps its own one orange part.

derivation.consequence: printing is flat on the material, with no shadow and no emboss
derivation.form: The name, the steps and the small word scene are flat ink on the card, and the card itself is a thin stock with the short unit shadow, never a raised key.

derivation.consequence: one grotesk, regular and medium only; hierarchy by size and position
derivation.form: The name is printed medium at body size on the top edge, the steps regular at caption size under it, so half the card out of a slot is still the name.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map (arrows step a detent, Home and End reach the ends, Space and Enter press) and a visible value and label
derivation.form: Enter picks the card up, an arrow or Tab reaches a slot, Enter there inserts it and Escape puts it back; the printed handle drags it as the pointer shortcut.

derivation.consequence: shadows are short and soft; a unit never floats more than its material height
derivation.form: A held card rises by one rise step with a key's short shadow and an ink mark under it, never a floating glowing tile.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The card is three keys wide and four keys tall, and its printed handle in the top corner keeps a full 44px square for a finger.

options.name: top-loading slit: a portrait card with the name on its top edge stands half out of a slit in the unit
side reader: a landscape ticket slides into a slot at the unit's side and sticks out past its end
dock bed: the whole card lies flat in a recessed bed on the unit

variants.reason: A keeps the name readable when inserted because it is printed on the edge that stays out (P5 hierarchy by size and position), and keeps the unit's outline fixed (P6); B cuts the name and breaks the body on a phone, and C is a drop zone holding a tile, which slides back to the scene grid.

root.why: The root holds the card and its hidden status, and keeps its place in the row while the card is held.

card.why: The card is light stock with dark ink in both themes and never orange, so the unit keeps one loud part.

name.why: The scene's name is printed medium at body size on the top edge, the part that stays out of a slot.

steps.why: What the scene does is printed under the name on the card's inset line, one short line per step.

step.why: Each step is a regular caption line in the same dark ink, so the card holds one ink at two sizes.

foot.why: The bottom row carries the small word scene at the start and the insert arrow at the end, on the inset line.

kind.why: The word scene is printed small and lowercase like a model name on a case, so the card says what it is.

arrow.why: A printed arrow on the bottom edge shows which end goes into the slot, flat ink and no emboss.

handle.why: The handle takes a 44px square in the top corner so a finger can drag the card while the keys do the same.

grip.why: The handle is six printed dots in the card's ink, flat on the stock like printing on a case.

announce.why: A polite hidden status says the card is picked up or put back, so holding a card is heard as well as seen.

hover.why: Hover only darkens the handle's dots, because a card does not rise when a pointer comes near it.

active.why: A pressed card drops its shadow at once, as a pressed part loses its height under the finger.

focus-visible.why: The focused card shows the same dark ring as every part in dial, offset so it clears the card's edge.

disabled.why: A scene that cannot run now lies flat with no shadow and cannot be picked up, keeping its words readable.

aria-pressed=true.why: A held card rises one rise step with a short key shadow and an ink mark under it, saying it is in the hand.

data-dragging=true.why: While dragged the card follows the pointer and lets the slot under it take the pointer, so the drop lands there.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduce motion the card does not rise or travel; the held mark and the shadow change at once.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the card keeps an outline and the held mark uses Highlight, because the stock and the shadow fade there.

transform.why: A picked card rises and settles back through the state motion tokens, fast in and slow out.

box-shadow.why: The shadow grows and shrinks with the rise on the same timing, so height and shadow move together.

opacity.why: The ink mark under a held card fades in on the state change instead of appearing in one frame.

color.why: The handle's dots darken on hover through the hover token and nothing else moves.
